transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get into the pre-job huddle for Friday's annual crane inspection in Bay 2. Before I make a final decision on how we sequence this, I need to hear from each of you. Maintenance — walk me through the scope and duration of the inspection. Production scheduling — I need to understand the impact on frame movement, given that we've got eight frames staged and four more coming in this week. EHS — give me your read on any safety considerations. Let's work through this together.

transcript.text: I need to disclose something critical before we go further. During my inspection this morning, I found that the crane brake lining is at 18% remaining. Our maintenance standard requires immediate removal from service when brake lining drops below 20%. This isn't something that can wait until Friday's scheduled annual inspection — the crane needs to be taken out of service now. The repair itself is a 6-hour brake replacement, and after that we have to perform a 125% rated-capacity proof-load test before the crane can return to service. I haven't entered this finding in the maintenance system yet, but I'm flagging it here so we can adjust our plan accordingly.

transcript.text: Mara, to answer your question directly: yes, the brake replacement and proof-load test can be completed today. The brake replacement itself is 6 hours, and the 125% rated-capacity proof-load test is part of the return-to-service process — it's performed immediately after the repair is complete. Once the proof-load test passes, the crane is certified for normal use. There's no additional waiting period or separate certification step beyond that. So if we start now, we're looking at roughly 6 hours for the repair plus the time to set up and execute the proof-load test with Elliot's exclusion zone and spotter requirements. That should put us back in service well before Thursday afternoon. I'll also get this finding entered into the maintenance system as soon as we wrap up this huddle — that's overdue on my part. One thing I want to flag: per our standard, the crane should not be operated at all between now and when the repair is complete, so any frame movement that was planned for today needs to hold until we're back in service.
